data.title: Power Corp. Earnings Call Highlights Strong Growth and Returns
data.description:
Power Corp Of Canada ((TSE:POW)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Power Corp.’s third-quarter call was strongly constructive, with broad earnings growth, record operating metrics, rising net asset value and substantial shareholder returns. Weakness in some NAV-based businesses, higher corporate costs, ChinaAMC’s asset decline and a still-material NAV discount were notable, but the positive developments outweighed the challenges.

Adjusted Earnings and EPS Growth

Power Corp. reported third-quarter adjusted net earnings of $964 million, up 12% from a year earlier. Adjusted earnings per share rose 13% to $1.53, supported by strong momentum at Great-West and IGM.

Great-West Delivers Strong Results

Great-West contributed $905 million to Power’s adjusted net earnings, a 7% year-over-year increase. Its base EPS rose 11% to $1.48, while base return on equity reached a record 19.4%, above its medium-term target for a third consecutive quarter.

Empower Maintains Operating Momentum

Empower’s base earnings increased 15% year over year on a constant-currency basis, with Retirement Services client assets reaching $2.15 trillion. Empower Wealth earnings climbed 28%, while its pretax base operating margin improved by 410 basis points.

IGM Reports a Record Quarter

IGM posted record third-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.51, up 19% year over year and ahead of its medium-term growth target of more than 9%. Wealth Management was a key contributor to the stronger result.

IGM Wealth Management Expands

IGM’s Wealth Management business grew 30% year over year, with assets under management and advisement rising 14% to $178 billion. The division recorded a third-quarter high for new client gross inflows, while net flows at IG Wealth and Mackenzie, including Northleaf, reached $3.4 billion.

IGM Boosts Returns and Investments

IGM returned more than $1 billion to shareholders during the first nine months through $585 million of buybacks and $421 million of dividends. It raised its Northleaf ownership to about 61%, while its Wealthsimple stake was valued at $2.9 billion.

Investment Fund Sales Improve

IGM investment fund net sales rose to $664 million from $407 million in the same quarter last year. The increase points to improving investor demand across its fund platform.

Rockefeller and Northleaf Grow

Rockefeller’s client assets increased 27% year over year to $236.5 billion. Northleaf’s client assets rose 10% to just under $38 billion, adding scale to Power’s alternative investment platform.

Wealthsimple Adds Clients and Assets

Wealthsimple’s assets under administration rose to $170 billion from $155 billion in the previous quarter, helped by about $11 billion in net flows. The platform added 200,000 clients and now serves approximately 4 million Canadians, while Power’s collective interest was valued at $5 billion net of carry.

NAV and Cash Position Strengthen

Power’s net asset value per share reached $113.28 at the end of the quarter, up 57% year over year, and stood at $120.20 as of the night before the call. Cash and equivalents totaled $1.9 billion, including $1.6 billion available after dividends receivable and payable, while public companies represented 90% of gross asset value.

Shareholder Returns Accelerate

Power returned $2.4 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks in the first nine months, compared with $1.5 billion a year earlier. Since 2020, total distributions through these channels have exceeded $13 billion.

Great-West Retains Capital Flexibility

Great-West repurchased nearly $1.3 billion of its shares year to date and held $2.8 billion in cash after accounting for a planned bond repayment. Power said it still intends to participate proportionately in Great-West’s additional $1.6 billion buyback program.

GBL Simplifies Its Portfolio

GBL has completed more than €5 billion of disposals involving listed companies and noncore assets. It returned €888 million through buybacks and dividends year to date and has set a 12-month goal of returning about €1 billion, without needing asset sales for liquidity.

Alternative Platforms Continue Scaling

Power’s alternative asset management platforms ended the quarter with $71.4 billion in assets under management. Sagard raised about C$1.4 billion during the quarter and nearly C$4 billion year to date, while increasing its economic interest in HalseyPoint to 60%.

Power Sustainable Plans Major Investment

Power Sustainable plans to invest and mobilize more than $10 billion in Canadian projects and companies over the next five years. Its infrastructure funds advanced new financing, capital recycling and renewable energy and storage opportunities across North America.

Management Emphasizes Active Ownership

Management described active ownership in strategy, capital allocation, leadership and risk management as a core value-creation tool. It is also focusing on artificial intelligence to help operating companies capture opportunities, building on earlier efforts in fintech and digitalization.

Proprietary Investments Produce Solid Returns

Power said returns on proprietary investments and co-investments supporting its alternative platforms exceeded 10% over the past one-, three- and five-year periods. The results reinforce the contribution of these investments beyond Power’s listed holdings.

NAV Discount Narrows

Power’s NAV discount narrowed to roughly 20% during the quarter, while NAV has grown at a 19% compound annual rate since 2020. Management said shareholder returns have materially outperformed both the S&P/TSX Financials Index and the broader S&P/TSX Composite across multiple time periods.

Some NAV Businesses Remain Challenged

GBL and Power Sustainable reported adjusted losses broadly in line with previous periods. These results highlight the earnings volatility that can accompany Power’s NAV-based and alternative businesses.

Sagard Earnings Face Investment Pressure

Sagard’s results were affected by lower earnings from investing activities, an investment loss and carried-interest expense linked to the rise in Wealthsimple’s value. These items weighed on reported earnings despite continued fundraising progress.

Corporate Costs Increase

Corporate operations and other activities produced a $107 million loss, including $61 million of operating expenses. Costs increased from the prior quarter because of higher performance-based compensation tied to strong operating results and Power’s higher share price.

ChinaAMC Assets Decline

ChinaAMC assets decreased 5% on a local-currency basis during the quarter. Management attributed the decline to weaker local markets rather than a broad deterioration across Power’s operating businesses.

Carried Interest Creates Volatility

Carried interest is recorded as an expense, creating an earnings drag when Wealthsimple’s value increases. Management said the net carry figure is difficult to forecast and can shift significantly, although current Wealthsimple share losses could eventually become a share of earnings.

Sagard Fee Earnings Remain Uneven

Market conditions and rate volatility continue to make fundraising, capital deployment and monetization difficult for Sagard. Although fee-related earnings were positive for two quarters, management cautioned that the measure will be volatile and will not be positive every quarter.

Discount Still Leaves Room for Improvement

Despite narrowing to about 20%, Power’s NAV discount remains material. Management said it is focused on growing NAV, increasing the dividend, simplifying the company and building more sustainable earnings.

Simplification Depends on Market Conditions

Potential transactions, including consolidating Wealthsimple ownership, would require willing buyers and sellers, sensible financing and clear benefits for shareholders. Management said such opportunities cannot be scheduled, while other possibilities include combining businesses or capabilities held in different parts of the group.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management said Great-West and IGM are exceeding their adjusted EPS growth targets, supporting expected low- to mid-teen returns including dividends. Great-West plans another $1.6 billion buyback, while Sagard is targeting US$100 billion of assets over the next several years and expects sustainable fee-related earnings and margins to improve directionally toward 2027.

GBL aims to return about €1 billion through buybacks and dividends over the next 12 months, while Power continues to target a 10% return on proprietary investments. Power’s own buybacks are expected to begin with a base range similar to recent years, from a few hundred million dollars up to about $400 million, with further direction from Great-West’s program.

Power Corp.’s call showed a company benefiting from strong performance at Great-West and IGM, growing wealth platforms and a sharp rise in NAV. While alternative earnings, corporate expenses and the discount to NAV remain concerns, substantial cash generation, capital returns and long-term growth initiatives kept the overall message firmly positive.

data.title: FRMO Corporation Earnings Call Balances Losses and Opportunity
data.description:
FRMO Corporation ((FRMO)) has held its Q1 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

FRMO Corporation’s earnings call delivered a mixed message. Strong cash generation, a debt-free balance sheet and a wide range of investment opportunities supported management’s confidence in the long term, but a $121 million quarterly loss, falling asset values and limited visibility into private holdings highlighted significant near-term risks.

Cash Flow and Debt-Free Balance Sheet

FRMO generated more than $600,000 in operating cash flow during the first quarter, compared with just under $5 million for the latest completed fiscal year. The company also held more than $46 million in cash, carried no debt and reported only nominal current liabilities.

Digital Assets Partly Offset Investment Losses

Bitcoin, Winland and other cryptocurrency-related funds in FRMO’s portfolio each rose by more than 40% during the quarter. Those gains helped offset losses elsewhere, although they were not enough to prevent a substantial consolidated decline.

Tax Benefit From Unrealized Losses

FRMO recorded a $19 million income tax benefit for the quarter. The benefit was primarily linked to lower deferred tax liabilities resulting from unrealized investment losses.

Zcash Mining Opportunity

Management described Zcash mining as “wildly profitable” and said the first machines purchased around May or June were expected to recover their costs rapidly. It also said that, if current profitability continued, the machines could generate roughly a 100% return over 1.5 years.

Investment Activity Continues

FRMO and Horizon Kinetics continue to make investments, evaluate new opportunities and discuss transactions involving private and public companies. Management also disclosed a small position in a company it estimates is trading at 30% to 40% of liquidation value, with plans to build the holding.

Cash Reserve Creates Flexibility

Management said FRMO’s large cash balance is not intended to remain idle indefinitely. The funds could support direct investments, private-market opportunities, strategic capital allocation, or efforts to seed businesses and establish new relationships.

Exposure to Compute Infrastructure

FRMO has investments in businesses connected to resources needed for expanding compute infrastructure. Management highlighted suitable land, water, natural-gas access, permitting and stable regulation as assets that could give the portfolio a role in the broader technology ecosystem.

CNSX Expansion and Tokenization

The Canadian Securities Exchange listed its first two exchange-traded funds in August and discussed five additional companies in a September release. Management also described a venture involving CNSX and Tetra Digital Group that could combine custody, a Canadian-dollar stablecoin, blockchain infrastructure and a regulated exchange for future asset tokenization.

Consensus Mining Ownership and Buybacks

FRMO held 28,910 Consensus Mining shares directly and indirectly on a look-through basis as of September 30. Consensus Mining adopted a $5 million repurchase program in May and bought back about 3% of its shares during the quarter ended June 30.

Winland Strategic Plan

FRMO owned 46% of Winland as of September 30, and management said its long-standing plan to eventually obtain control had not changed. However, any ownership increase or future consolidation remains dependent on events that management did not specify.

Organizational Simplification

Management said FRMO has further flattened its organization while reviewing products and communications for possible streamlining. Technology is being used to improve workflows, younger employees have been given more freedom to pursue opportunities, and a single-floor office has improved collaboration.

Fiscal Year-End Change

FRMO moved its fiscal year-end from May 31 to June 30 to simplify reporting and align with common quarter-end dates. Management expects the change to improve the timeliness and comparability of information while making administration and auditing more efficient.

Private Investment Pipeline

The company is evaluating private-market opportunities, including non-metals-based industrial and electrification-scale batteries and large water-supply ventures. Management also referenced the Horizon Kinetics Royalty and Real Asset Fund, which invests in private assets such as oil, gas and water-related opportunities.

Management Remains Positive on Holdings

Management said Murray Stahl has been particularly optimistic about the investment opportunity at FRMO and Horizon Kinetics. Peter Doyle said the underlying portfolio companies have substantial potential and could grow robustly over time, while acknowledging that returns may be uneven and cannot be guaranteed.

Crypto and Diversified Stores of Wealth

Management emphasized Bitcoin’s decentralized structure and said its ownership and transaction records could remain intact through a temporary system outage. FRMO also owns royalty companies and gold and silver miners, which management views as additional stores of wealth amid infrastructure and access risks.

Large Consolidated Net Loss

FRMO reported a consolidated first-quarter net loss of $121 million. The loss attributable to FRMO was approximately $36 million, or $0.81 per share, after excluding losses attributable to noncontrolling interests in Horizon Kinetics Hard Assets.

Investment Losses Drove Expenses

Consolidated other expenses totaled $140 million and were driven largely by a decline of more than 25% in TPL. MIAX fell nearly 10%, while Horizon Kinetics Holding Corporation declined 31% during the same three-month period, adding to the investment losses.

Assets and Hard Assets Results

Consolidated assets declined to $650 million at September 30 from $747 million at May 31, 2026, primarily because of lower market values for investments. Horizon Kinetics Hard Assets held just under $340 million in assets and lost $108.6 million, largely because of unrealized losses tied to TPL’s decline.

Advisory Fees Softened

Consulting and advisory fees were $800,000 in the first quarter. That figure represented a modest decrease from the comparable period a year earlier.

Large Acquisition Abandoned

Management said it had considered a sizable acquisition that would have expanded revenue and the shareholder base. The transaction was abandoned after its risk-reward profile failed to appear attractive enough, although the company continues to search for expansion opportunities.

Limited Visibility Into Private Holdings

FRMO said it could not provide significant operating updates on Synteq Digital and remained cautious when discussing private companies including Digital Currency Group and CNSX. Management noted public information about Synteq’s unified rental system for GPU servers, virtual machines and physical servers, launched at the end of July.

Winland Consolidation Timing Unclear

Although FRMO owns 46% of Winland and continues to seek a controlling interest, management declined to say whether consolidation would occur by year-end. It also provided no details on the timing or number of additional shares that might be purchased.

Infrastructure Risks Remain

Management acknowledged that outages and infrastructure constraints remain real risks, while FRMO’s internal systems require frequent patches as artificial intelligence identifies dormant software bugs. It also noted that crypto access depends on power and telecommunications, and that AI providers and hyperscalers face demanding reliability requirements.

No FRMO Share Repurchase Program

FRMO does not currently have a share repurchase program. Management said one could be introduced almost immediately after discussions with the board and indicated that the option would be considered.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management said Zcash machines bought around May or June could deliver roughly a 100% return over 1.5 years if current profitability persists, while another company trading at 30% to 40% of liquidation value could appreciate substantially over five to 10 years. The acquisition search continues, a potential investment could materially affect results, and management reiterated its plan to seek control of Winland without giving a timetable; the next report is expected in the first half of February.

FRMO’s call balanced severe market-driven losses against a strong balance sheet and an ambitious investment strategy. Investors are left with a financially resilient but volatile company whose long-term opportunities in digital assets, hard assets and infrastructure remain promising, while execution, valuation swings and limited disclosure create meaningful uncertainty.

data.title: Alps Group Regains Nasdaq Minimum Bid Price Compliance
data.description:
ALPS Group ( (ALPS) ) just unveiled an update.

On November 20, 2026, Alps Group said Nasdaq confirmed that it had regained compliance with the $1 minimum bid-price requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Global Market. The company said its closing bid price was $1 or greater for 10 consecutive business days from November 9 through November 20, 2026.

The announcement followed a 1-for-5 share consolidation, with post-consolidation trading beginning November 9, and a November 16 Nasdaq notice saying the shares faced delisting after the company failed to regain compliance by November 11. Nasdaq said the matter was closed, and the ordinary shares continued trading under the symbol ALPS.

data.title: PMV Pharmaceuticals Presents Updated PYNNACLE Trial Data
data.description:
PMV Pharmaceuticals ( (PMVP) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On November 20, 2026, PMV Pharmaceuticals reported updated data from the pivotal Phase 2 portion of the PYNNACLE trial, which evaluated rezatapopt monotherapy in patients with TP53 Y220C-mutated advanced solid tumors. The data were presented that day as a late-breaking oral presentation at ENA 2026 in Barcelona, Spain.

In 65 platinum-resistant or refractory ovarian cancer patients who had received prior standard care, investigator-assessed overall response rate was 48%, median duration of response was 10.4 months and disease control rate was 83%. Among 168 evaluable patients across all cohorts, overall response rate was 36% and median duration of response was 8.1 months; responses were observed across eight tumor types, while treatment-related adverse events were mostly Grade 1 or 2 and 11 patients discontinued treatment because of them.

data.title: GSK Transfers 22,000,000 Treasury Shares to Procure 11,000,000 ADRs
data.description:
GlaxoSmithKline ( (GSK) ) has provided an update.

GSK is a global biopharma company whose stated purpose is to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

On November 20, 2026, GSK transferred 22,000,000 treasury-held ordinary shares to JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., the depositary for its American depositary receipts programme, to procure the issuance and transfer of 11,000,000 ADRs to the GlaxoSmithKline (US) Trust. The ADRs were to be used to satisfy awards under the Deferred Annual Bonus Plan, Performance Share Plan and Share Value Plan.

The consideration received was $47.82 per ADR, or $23.91 per ordinary share, and was funded by a contribution to the Trust from GlaxoSmithKline LLC. Following the transfer, GSK will hold 248,881,064 ordinary shares in treasury and have 4,067,451,066 ordinary shares in issue, excluding treasury shares; treasury shares will represent 6.12% of voting rights.
